correctness.rationale: Every projection onto ker(sum) is I-sigma(.)v with sum v=1. Averaging coordinate permutations makes the centering P=I-J/n norm-minimal. Decreasing-magnitude layer cake represents each x as nonnegative linear combination of signed support indicators, giving exact finite max P-norm/W_k. Norm one is equivalent to t=0 minimizing N_w(y+t1) for each y with sum zero. For generic y the derivative vanishes iff all feasible sorted sign words have weighted sum zero. Positive gap variables show feasibility iff a prefix signed sum is negative. Enumerating feasible words yields the n=2,3,4 equalities; for n>=5 comparing all continuations of (+,-,-) forces tail weights zero, and (+,+,-,-,-,...) contradicts w1>0 with monotonicity. Independently enumerated signed supports and exact integer weight families for n=2..6 support this. Finite test does not prove n>6.

value.rationale: This is a natural symmetric hyperplane projection constant for weighted rearrangement norms. An exact all-n signed-support maximum and sharp dimension-four cutoff are structurally useful, not arbitrary small-size enumeration; zero tail weights and full real-weight quantification matter.

final_claim: For real N_w(x)=sum_{j=1}^n w_j |x|_(j) with nonincreasing w_j>=0,w1>0, the coordinate-sum-zero hyperplane admits a norm-one projection exactly when n=2, or n=3 with w1=w2+w3, or n=4 with w1=w2+w3 and w4=0; none exist for n>=5. The optimal norm is given for all n by a finite maximum over signed-support indicators.
